items.review_rationale: Read the multiplicative-order-exactly-n condition for a primitive root and distinguished it from merely satisfying ζ^n=1. The ambient multiplication is in the field's unit group.

references.context: Least positive integer m for which ζ^m=1 in the group F×; primitive nth root requires order exactly n

references.disposition: Exact order rules out proper divisor orders even though such elements also satisfy ζ^n=1.

items.review_rationale: Read a generic point of an irreducible closed subset via the closure of its singleton, explicitly preserving the ambient topological space and irreducibility of the closed target subset.

references.phrase: irreducible subset Z with subspace topology
irreducible closed subset Z of X
references.context: Nonempty subset closed in X whose induced topology is irreducible; not necessarily an entire irreducible component

references.disposition: The equality defines the generic-point property and is not a requirement that η be a unique point without sobriety.

items.review_rationale: Read an irreducible component as an irreducible subset maximal by inclusion, and kept the fact that maximal such subsets are closed as a derived property rather than requiring arbitrary closed subsets in the maximizing family.

references.context: An irreducible subset not properly contained in any other irreducible subset of the ambient X

references.disposition: Closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible, so inclusion-maximal irreducible subsets are closed.

items.review_rationale: Read irreducibility as a nonempty topological space that cannot be the union of two proper closed subsets. Distinguished the nonempty convention and equivalently overlapping nonempty open-set property without declaring it another definition.

references.phrase: closed subset of a topological space
references.context: Complement of an open subset in X under the specified topology

references.phrase: union of two proper closed subsets
references.context: Set-theoretic union A∪B=X with A,B each closed and not equal to X

references.disposition: An empty space is explicitly excluded from irreducibility in this formulation even though alternative conventions may exist.

references.phrase: cannot be written as union of two proper closed subsets
references.disposition: The definition rules out any such pair, not merely disjoint closed decompositions.
